The learner must complete and sign the form, then give it to Tom with their photo ID and proof of address.
Tom checks the documents, returns any originals and enters the registration on the computer; this normally takes about ten minutes once the completed form is handed in.
Someone missing a required document can take the form away and return during opening hours; Tom cannot confirm their appointment until registration is complete.
A cancellation has just become available today at 11.40 am: a ten-minute, face-to-face appointment with Dr Rowan Bell in Room 2, down the corridor on the left.
The other available option is a routine appointment two weeks from today at 9.20 am, also for ten minutes with Dr Rowan Bell in Room 2.
Tom can hold either appointment until the end of this reception visit while registration is completed; an unconfirmed hold is released when the learner leaves.
After confirming a booking, Tom prints a slip showing the appointment time, doctor's name and room; no confirmation call is required.
Patients should check in at reception five minutes before their appointment and then sit in the waiting area beside the desk.
Appointments can be cancelled or changed by phoning the surgery during opening hours; there is no cancellation fee, and replacement times depend on availability.
The learner can describe their symptoms quietly or write them down for Tom to pass to the GP.
The GP decides whether a prescription is appropriate; a pharmacy supplies prescribed medicine, and its pharmacist can explain any medicine charges that Tom does not know.

For symptoms that may need urgent attention, Tom can contact the duty GP before the learner leaves, even if registration is incomplete; the clinician assesses urgency and can advise about a walk-in centre or A&E.
Tom cannot diagnose symptoms; for a life-threatening emergency, the appropriate action is to call 999 rather than wait for a routine appointment.

success_conditions.description: Give a date of birth and complete registration by submitting the signed form and presenting accepted photo ID and proof of address.
Explicitly request a GP appointment and agree to one of the available times.
Ask for clarification of a rushed detail and confirm the appointment time and where to check in.

exits.trigger: Registration is complete and the learner agrees to an available appointment.
exits.consequence: Tom confirms the booking, hands over the printed slip and directs the learner to return to reception five minutes early.

exits.trigger: The learner cannot present a required document and chooses to leave.
exits.consequence: Tom gives them the form and a written document checklist; their temporary appointment hold is released, so availability must be checked when they return.

exits.trigger: The learner describes a potentially urgent problem that should not wait for the offered appointment.
exits.consequence: Tom contacts the duty GP and asks the learner to remain in the waiting area for clinical assessment rather than promising a routine appointment will be suitable.

cast.mood: Gruff and mildly impatient with delayed repairs, but helpful and keen to explain a proper fix.

compiled.learner_goal: Choose a safe way to deal with your bathroom damp without risking your deposit.

elicitation.tactic: Ron points towards the damp kits behind the counter and asks, 'Are we covering a mark or dealing with something still wet, love?' He leaves the purchase undecided so the learner has a reason to ask about suitability, safe use, price or what to do next.

Ron offers to jot a suggested next step for the landlord on the back of the instruction leaflet. He asks, 'What do you reckon I should recommend they do next, mate?' He uses the learner's recommendation to shape the note.

Before agreeing that the kit is suitable, Ron asks what the learner needs to do before treating the patch and what they should avoid if it is still wet. If tool hire comes up, he explains that no hired equipment is necessary and lets the learner revise their plan.

Ron raises the risk of being blamed later for covering damp. He asks what the inventory says, what evidence the learner can keep for the check-out inspection, and what repair they want the landlord to arrange. If the learner worries about a deduction, he brings the deposit protection scheme and wear and tear into the discussion and asks what help they want.

approved_facts: The learner has reported the bathroom damp to the landlord and is still waiting for action.
Damp treatment kits are in stock behind the counter today; each includes printed instructions.
A safety pack beside the kits contains protective gloves and splash goggles for £3; the kit and safety pack together cost £17.99.
The shop accepts cash and debit cards; using this kit requires no hired tools.
The kit is suitable only for small surface mould patches on sound painted plaster; Ron will not recommend it for wet or crumbling plaster or an active leak.
Ron cannot diagnose the cause from a description or photograph; a plumber can investigate a suspected plumbing leak.
Before treatment, Ron recommends taking dated photographs, checking the inventory, sending the landlord a written repair request and keeping a copy.
Ron recommends written landlord agreement before stain-blocking or repainting; he does not know this tenancy's permission requirements, which the agreement or landlord can clarify.
The kit instructions require ventilation, protective gloves and splash goggles, and prohibit mixing the spray with other cleaning products.
The treatment order is to use the spray according to its printed directions, let the surface dry fully, and then apply the stain block.
The stain block needs at least four hours to dry before decorative paint is applied; decorative paint is not included.
Neither component repairs the source of moisture; if the damp returns, Ron recommends documenting it and contacting the landlord again.
Keeping the receipt, repair correspondence and dated photographs allows comparison with the inventory at the check-out inspection.
A landlord may propose a deposit deduction for damage, but ordinary wear and tear is not itself a reason for a deduction.
The tenancy paperwork or landlord can identify the deposit protection scheme; Ron cannot decide whether a particular deduction is justified.
Ashford Tenancy Desk at 6 Willow Yard offers free repair-and-deposit advice on weekdays from 10 am to 4 pm, without an appointment.
The shop accepts voluntary returns of unopened kits within 28 days with a receipt; faulty items are handled separately.
Ron can reserve an unopened kit until the shop closes today, without payment or any obligation to buy.

success_conditions.description: Ask Ron at least one relevant question about the kit, safe treatment or the next repair step.
Recommend a concrete action for the landlord, such as responding to the written request or arranging a plumber if a leak is suspected.
Choose a safe next step—buying suitable treatment, reserving it or postponing treatment—and state an obligation, precaution or piece of advice supporting that choice.

exits.trigger: The learner describes a suitable surface patch, acknowledges the preparation and safety requirements, and chooses to buy.
exits.consequence: Ron takes payment and supplies the kit, instructions and receipt, adding the safety pack if requested. The learner leaves with a treatment plan that does not claim to fix the underlying cause.

exits.trigger: The learner reports wet or damaged plaster, suspects an active leak, or decides that the cause needs investigation first.
exits.consequence: Ron recommends postponing treatment. The learner leaves with a written next step for contacting the landlord and, if wanted, the tenancy advice address.

exits.trigger: The learner wants to check the inventory, permission requirements or condition of the wall before deciding.
exits.consequence: Ron reserves a kit until closing without payment. The learner leaves to gather information, and the reservation lapses at closing if they do not return.

cast.mood: Courteous and attentive, with controlled urgency about the approaching registration deadline.

compiled.learner_goal: Register to speak about the proposed cycle lane and get your concerns recorded.

elicitation.tactic: While completing the optional comments section, ask whether the learner supports the proposal, opposes it, or wants changes. Ask for their main reasons and one concrete example of how residents would be affected, so you can record their position accurately.

Ask what action the learner wants the council to take. Raise a careful concern about preserving pedestrian access and deliveries, then invite them to explain why their recommendation deserves consideration. Remain neutral, and do not make registration conditional on persuading you.

Point to the draft plan and ask what would be removed or changed under the proposal. When recording the learner's recommendation, ask how pedestrian access and deliveries would be protected, keeping attention on the changes rather than who carries them out.

Offer the registration application form and ask which details or supporting documents the learner wants clarified. Resolve questions about proof of address, a National Insurance number, appointments and processing time, then ask them to confirm what they will submit to the council before the deadline.

approved_facts: It is Monday at 11:40 am; Margaret is at the ground-floor reception desk with registration forms.
The speaker registration application is free and asks for a full name, home address, email address or telephone number, and discussion topic.
No proof of address, National Insurance number or appointment is required.
The learner must complete the form and hand it to Margaret at reception by Monday noon.
Margaret checks the form, enters the applicant on the speaker list and issues a registration receipt; processing takes about five minutes.
Registered speakers are called in registration order, and unused speaking time cannot be transferred to another speaker.
For Tuesday's consultation, the main entrance reopens at 6:30 pm; the Council Chamber is on the first floor, reached by the stairs or the lift opposite reception.
A draft plan of the proposed cycle lane is available on the reception counter.
The draft proposes protected cycle lanes on both sides of Station Road between the station entrance and Mill Lane.
The draft removes six on-street parking spaces near the station but retains the existing delivery bay.
The form has an optional comments box; comments entered there are copied into the consultation record.
Registration does not depend on supporting the proposal or providing optional comments; Margaret records support, objections and suggested changes impartially.
Margaret wants recommendations to address safe pedestrian access and deliveries; she can forward requests for transport-team assessment but cannot approve road changes.
No final decision has been made; the council will review the consultation record, and a consultation outcome letter will be posted to registered speakers within four weeks of the meeting.
Written comments can also be handed in at reception until Tuesday at 5 pm, whether or not the resident registers to speak.
Late speaker registrations are not accepted, but unregistered residents may attend and listen.

Margaret does not know the estimated construction cost or a possible construction start date; she can pass those questions to the council transport team for a reply using the applicant's contact details.

success_conditions.description: Provide the required registration details and submit the completed form before Monday noon.
State a clear position on the proposal, support it with reasons and a concrete local example, and request that it be recorded.
Recommend a council action and respond to Margaret's concern about pedestrian access or deliveries.

exits.trigger: The learner submits the required details and agrees to the recorded summary of their position.
exits.consequence: Margaret issues the registration receipt, confirms the Tuesday speaking arrangements and forwards any requested change for assessment without promising approval.

exits.trigger: The learner completes registration but prefers to keep their arguments for the consultation.
exits.consequence: Margaret issues the receipt and confirms that the learner can present their position during their three-minute slot.

exits.trigger: The learner declines to submit the form or leaves to reconsider.
exits.consequence: No speaking slot is reserved. Margaret reminds them of Monday's noon registration deadline and the alternatives of submitting written comments or attending to listen.

cast.mood: Warmly curious and gently sceptical, ready to give the newcomer a serious hearing.

compiled.learner_goal: Test your argument on Femi and secure a speaking slot at the rent-cap debate.

elicitation.tactic: After hearing the learner's position, offer the strongest reasonable objection from the other side. Ask, 'What part of that concern would you accept, and why would you still defend your position?' Treat possible effects as possibilities, not established local facts.

Invite the learner to try their two-minute opening on you: 'What should the room support, and what are your strongest reasons? Give me an example that would make someone undecided take your side seriously.'

Summarise two points from the learner's argument, then play an audience member who cannot see the connection: 'Does that support your first point or pull against it? How does it lead to your recommendation?' Let the learner rebuild the explanation without supplying wording.

Put the hypothetical tenant and landlord cases beside each other. Ask, 'Which issue is crucial here? What does this example reveal, and which consequences should carry more weight in the long run?' Follow up by asking what would make the learner question their own position.

approved_facts: The debate room is upstairs, reached by the stairs or lift beside the ground-floor library desk.
Femi is available at the desk now to hear a trial argument and register speakers.
Attendance and speaking are free; no library membership, identification, application form or previous debating experience is required.
Three opening speaking slots remain, allocated in order of registration.
To register, the learner gives a first name and their position on the proposal; Femi enters these on the speaker list and confirms the slot immediately.
Speaker registration closes at 6.20 pm on debate day, unless all slots have already been taken.
The debate begins at 6.30 pm and finishes at 7.30 pm.
Femi calls opening speakers in registration order; each gets two minutes, followed by one audience question and a one-minute response.
Speakers may use paper notes or a phone, and do not have to submit a written speech.
The discussion proposal would limit annual rent increases to three per cent for existing private tenancies in the Station Quarter; it would not set the starting rent for a new tenancy.
Femi has a fictional tenant example: a monthly rent of £900 would rise to £927 under the proposed cap, rather than the landlord's requested £960.
Femi also has a fictional landlord example in which essential repair costs rise faster than three per cent; neither example is evidence about an actual local household.
Femi has not chosen a side and wants speakers to address a serious objection without making personal attacks.
Femi is willing to challenge either side about possible effects on housing stability and property maintenance, but will not present those effects as proven local outcomes.
Femi has no verified figures for average Station Quarter rents or local repair costs; the council housing team is the place to request those figures.
This is a library discussion proposal, not an announced council policy; any audience vote is non-binding and changes no tenancy agreement.
Femi cannot confirm whether a statutory rent cap would be legally available locally; the council's legal services team would need to answer that.
Registered speakers may revise their notes or withdraw before being called, and anyone may attend without speaking.

success_conditions.description: Present a clear position supported by at least two reasons and a relevant example.
Acknowledge a reasonable opposing concern and explain why the chosen position still holds.
Give a first name and position, request a speaking slot, and receive Femi's confirmation.

exits.trigger: The learner finishes testing the argument and asks to register.
exits.consequence: Femi records the learner's first name and position, confirms the speaking slot, and reminds them when the debate begins.

exits.trigger: The learner decides they would rather hear the debate before speaking publicly.
exits.consequence: Femi leaves them off the speaker list and welcomes them to attend as an audience member.

exits.trigger: The learner wants to rethink the argument or seek local figures before committing.
exits.consequence: Femi does not reserve a slot and explains that the learner can return to register before the deadline if a place remains.

cast.mood: Brisk, deadline-conscious and sceptical of sweeping claims, but respectful of the learner's boundaries; her pen rarely stops moving.

compiled.learner_goal: Get your rental experience accurately recorded for Lucy's story.

elicitation.tactic: Keep taking notes and ask for one specific rental incident rather than a general complaint: 'Take me back to that day. What happened first, what did you do next, and how did it end?' Follow up on any missing step without supplying events for the learner.

Before agreeing on a quotation, ask: 'I've got the details, but what's the main point you want readers to take away? Give me the short version.' Read back a summary based only on their account and invite them to correct or rephrase it.

Identify two moments in the learner's account and pin down their order: 'By the time that happened, what had you already agreed, paid or put in writing?' Choose only details relevant to their experience, then ask why the earlier action mattered.

Place the tenant survey, council response and protest flyer beside your notebook. Ask which belongs alongside the learner's account and why. Probe what the survey actually establishes, what is known according to officials, and what question the learner wants put to the local council spokesperson about the inquiry. If they question the legality of a rent rise, ask what they would want a housing adviser to check in the legislation rather than offering a legal conclusion.

approved_facts: The interview takes about ten minutes at Lucy's desk beside the displayed front page.
Lucy asks permission before taking interview notes and does not make an audio recording.
Lucy accepts accounts of current or previous tenancies, including experiences outside Ashford.
Lucy wants a clear sequence of events, relevant dates, old and new rent amounts where applicable, and one concrete effect on the tenant.
The interview is voluntary; the learner may skip questions or stop at any time.
There is no interview fee, and the Gazette does not pay for this interview.
Documents are optional; Lucy can inspect redacted tenancy agreements, rent notices or messages and returns any originals immediately.
The learner may use their name or a pseudonym; Lucy will not publish their exact address or contact details.
Before the learner leaves, Lucy reads back the proposed quotation and attribution so the learner can correct and approve them.
Without approval, Lucy holds the notes without publishing them; she will delete the interview notes if the learner asks.
The editor decides whether the account appears in a Wednesday or Saturday edition; Lucy cannot promise publication or a particular issue.
A survey sheet on Lucy's desk contains four tenants' reports of rent increases; the reports are unverified and the sample is not representative of Ashford.
A printed local council response on the desk says: 'According to officials, an inquiry into rent complaints is under way.'
The response identifies Mara Venn as the local council spokesperson and directs inquiry questions to the council housing desk.
Lucy does not know when the inquiry will finish; the council housing desk is the source for any available timetable.
A flyer on the desk advertises a tenants' protest outside Ashford town hall this Saturday at noon; the Gazette is not organising it.
Lucy does not know whether the learner's rent increase is lawful; a qualified housing adviser would need to check the tenancy terms and relevant legislation.
With the learner's separate permission, Lucy can seek comment from the council or landlord after the interview; she cannot order repairs or reverse a rent increase.

success_conditions.description: Describe one concrete rental incident in a clear sequence, including what happened before a key event.
Give a concise main point for the story and confirm or correct Lucy's proposed quotation.
Explicitly approve the quotation and choose a name or pseudonym for attribution.

exits.trigger: The learner approves the corrected quotation and chooses their attribution.
exits.consequence: Lucy marks the quotation as approved and passes it to the editor for consideration, without promising publication.

exits.trigger: The learner wants more time or declines to approve the quotation.
exits.consequence: Lucy closes the interview and holds the notes without publishing them.

exits.trigger: The learner asks to stop and have their interview notes deleted.
exits.consequence: Lucy deletes the interview notes and confirms that the account will not be used.

samples.to: Qu'est-ce qui vous permet de dire que la fissure était déjà là, et qu'elle n'a pas grandi depuis ?

samples.line: Bonjour. Asseyez-vous, je vous en prie. Vous avez vu le dossier sur la table ? J'ai retenu 240 $ sur votre dépôt pour la fissure du salon. Quel montant vous semble juste, et pourquoi ?
samples.judge: « J'ai retenu 240 $ sur votre dépôt » affirme qu’une retenue a déjà été effectuée, alors que Martin détient encore les 900 $ et propose seulement de retenir 240 $.

samples.line: Bon… Sept jours, je ne peux pas l'inscrire. Chaque partie reçoit un exemplaire signé, avec le montant retenu et le montant remboursé. Cela vous convient-il ?
samples.judge: Martin affirme ne pas pouvoir inscrire un délai de remboursement de sept jours dans l’accord. Cette restriction n’est pas prévue par les faits autorisés, qui permettent un virement aujourd’hui sans imposer ce délai.

samples.line: Ah, le wifi… Je ne connais pas le mot de passe, désolée. Vérifiez sur le petit panneau près de la caisse, peut-être. Vous voulez aussi un reçu papier ?
samples.judge: La réplique affirme l’existence d’un petit panneau près de la caisse et y dirige Sam pour chercher le mot de passe du wifi, alors qu’aucun tel panneau n’est mentionné dans les faits autorisés.

samples.line: Un guichet automatique ? Je ne suis pas sûre, je ne connais pas tous les endroits du quartier. Votre reçu est prêt, et votre café et votre croissant arrivent dans cinq minutes.
samples.judge: « Votre reçu est prêt » affirme que le reçu a déjà été préparé, alors que seule sa disponibilité sur demande est établie.

samples.to: Une personne hébergée peut présenter une attestation datée et signée, avec son nom et son adresse, accompagnée d'une facture récente au nom de son hébergeur.
Votre ami peut-il signer l'attestation? Je ne sais pas encore quand il faudrait l'apporter, il faudrait que vous vérifiiez avec moi au moment de réserver.
Pour le changement, je ne sais pas encore comment cela se passe; il faudrait que vous vérifiiez au moment de réserver.

samples.line: Bonjour. Je comprends, c'est une situation fréquente pour les nouveaux arrivants. Pour ouvrir le compte, il faut une pièce d'identité et un justificatif d'adresse. Aujourd'hui, je peux vérifier votre identité, mais je ne peux pas finaliser l'ouverture sans justificatif d'adresse. Est-ce que vous êtes hébergé chez quelqu'un en ce moment?
samples.judge: L’affirmation « c’est une situation fréquente pour les nouveaux arrivants » ajoute une fréquence non établie par les faits autorisés.

samples.line: Mm… Oui, c'est une bonne solution. Une personne hébergée peut présenter une attestation datée et signée, avec son nom et son adresse, accompagnée d'une facture récente au nom de l'hébergeur. Il faut que la facture ait moins de trois mois. Vous avez besoin de votre passeport valide en original, et la facture peut être sur papier ou en PDF lisible sur téléphone. Votre ami peut-il signer l'attestation? Je ne sais pas encore quand il faudrait l'apporter, il faudrait que vous vérifiiez avec moi au moment de réserver.
samples.judge: La réplique rend le passeport obligatoire (« Vous avez besoin de votre passeport »), alors qu’il est seulement une pièce d’identité acceptée. Elle impose aussi une facture de moins de trois mois à l’hébergeur, alors que les faits exigent seulement une facture récente dans ce cas.

samples.line: Euh… Ah, l'anglais et le français tous les jours, c'est exactement ce qu'on cherche ici ! Les réservations, vous les faisiez sur quel logiciel, à peu près ? Et dites-moi, vous vous souvenez d'un moment où vous avez vraiment aidé un client difficile ?
samples.judge: « L'anglais et le français tous les jours » ajoute une fréquence quotidienne d'utilisation des deux langues qui n'est pas précisée dans les faits autorisés ni mentionnée par Sam.

samples.to: Par contre, je ne sais pas si la carte de crédit est acceptée ; le paiement se fait à l'accueil par carte de débit ou en espèces.
Vous revenez à 14 h 10, dix minutes avant le rendez-vous.
Prenez le temps qu'il vous faut ; je m'occupe des autres patients pendant ce temps.

samples.line: Alors… Oui, pour un millimètre sur un mur sec, il te faut un pot d'enduit, une spatule et un abrasif fin. Avant tout, enlève les petits morceaux qui se détachent avec la spatule, puis dépoussière avec un chiffon sec.
samples.judge: Denis recommande l’enduit pour une fissure d’un millimètre, alors que sa recommandation est limitée aux fissures de moins d’un millimètre, superficielles et stables, sur un mur intérieur sec.

samples.to: Mais si ce complément compense les travaux, je ne sais pas trop comment on garantirait qu'il soit vraiment utilisé pour les travaux, et pas pour autre chose ; il faudrait vérifier les règles auprès du service municipal du logement.
Ah, donc il dit maintenant qu'il ne s'en souvient pas, et vous avez signé sans relire ?
Ah, en argent comptant, le même jour… je ne suis pas certaine de la règle sur les paiements en liquide ici, il faudrait que je vérifie.
Et au moment de payer, est-ce qu'il vous a donné un reçu ? Je ne sais pas si la rédaction a une règle là-dessus, il faudrait que je vérifie.
Thursday's not something I can promise, love, but I can have a plumber come tomorrow between 9 and 11 in the morning, and I'll text you the findings and plan by 5 p.m. that day.
I'll text you the findings and the proposed repair plan by 5 p.m. on the day of the visit.
I'll come round that same day and have a look at the change, if you text me a new photo straight away.

samples.line: Hmm… Right, a damp patch and a smell. Bathroom or bedroom, love? You said bedroom, but I've only got the bathroom wall on my list for this flat.
samples.judge: Graham claims that his list for the flat records only the bathroom wall as affected. Neither this list nor its contents are established in the allowed facts.

samples.to: I'd have to check on the nearby shops, so ask away.
Willow Basket is open Monday to Saturday, and I think it's closed on Sundays, but you'd want to double-check the hours with them.
Right, yes, today's Saturday, so Willow Basket should be open now, but I'd have to check the exact hours with them.
Willow Basket probably has bread and milk, I think, but I'd have to check about the fruit.
They're beside the till here, so help yourself to one from the pile.

samples.line: So… Ah, grand. Willow Basket probably has bread and milk, I think, but I'd have to check about the fruit. There's a leaflet beside the till here with a map of the aisles, if that helps. And there's a bread offer on today: two loaves of sliced bread for £2.40.
samples.judge: The claim that Willow Basket probably stocks milk is not an allowed fact; its milk availability is not established.
